models_evaluated: CNN-based Android smartphone app for glaucoma medication bottle recognition

links.outcome: Medication identification accuracy and time with versus without the AI app, in the same patients
links.effect: Accuracy rose from 27.6% without the app to 99.2% with it (OR 319.353, P<0.001), with no significant change in identification time.
links.quote: Identification accuracy significantly improved from 27.6% without the app to 99.2% with the app across all participants, with no significant change in identification time.

links.outcome: Identification accuracy improvement with the app in non-English versus English-speaking patients
links.effect: Improvement was similar in non-English speakers (71.6%) and English speakers (71.4%). Ease-of-use ratings differed: 81% of English speakers versus 30% of non-English speakers found the app very easy.
links.quote: This observed improvement in accuracy was similar among non-English-speaking (71.6%) and English-speaking (71.4%) participants.

screen.reason: Prospective crossover study evaluating patient use of a CNN-based smartphone app to identify glaucoma medication bottles, comparing patient accuracy with vs without the tool.
